Sprengel 1830, vol. 2, pp. 561-562 (Comm. III cap. CXLVII): 'Duas Dioscorides enumerat species, marem iuglandis, et feminam smyrnii foliis. Illam habeo Paeoniam nostram officinalem, vel arietinam Anders. et peregrinam Mill., foliis subtus pubescentibus a priore distinctam: feminam vero P. corallinam Retz. Qui contrarium proferunt, haud sedulo comparasse foliorum formas videntur. Folia enim Smyrnii multo magis ad P. corallinae formam accedunt. Plures autem species et in Creta et in reliqua Graecia proveniunt.' Thus: MALE (walnut-like leaves) = P. officinalis / P. arietina Anders. / P. peregrina Mill.; FEMALE (Smyrnium-like leaves) = P. corallina Retz. Others assigned them the other way round (contrary opinion noted). Also notes γλυκυσίδη as a name reported by Theophrastus. | Fraas 1845, pp. 134-135 gives the REVERSE assignment: MALE παιωνία ἄρρην (Diosc. 3,147 'mas, foliis juglandis') = Paeonia corallina Retz. ('Daher zieht Sprengel - comment. in Dioscor. pag. 561 mit Unrecht die folgende hieher'); the commonest in Greece, on Delphi (Euboea), Parnassus, Oeta in the fir zone; FEMALE παιωνία ἡ γλυκυσίδη θήλεια = P. officinalis L., much rarer, mostly W Greece (Cyllene, Kalavryta). Sprengel 1830, vol. 2, p. 483 (Comm. II cap. CCIV): discusses names; 'Ceterum descriptio optima'; the very acrid caper from the Red Sea coast and Africa = perhaps Forsskål's Capparis redif s. oblongifolia. The species name for the main plant is given only in Index V, p. 702: 'Capparis spinosa L. 483' (and 'Capparis oblongifolia Forsk. 483'). Sprengel does not distinguish C. spinosa from C. orientalis (Linnaean C. spinosa s.l.). | Fraas 1845, p. 116: '1. Capparis spinosa L. var. ovata W., rundblättrige, gemeine Kapper' = κάππαρις Theophr., κάππαρις Diosc. 2,204 'der noch einige andere ausländische Arten anführt'; very common in plains, among stones and on rocks (C. rupestris on sea cliffs), Attica, Boeotia, Corinth, Argos; 'folia ovalia apice mucronulato - retusa'. Osbaldeston 2000, ch. 2-204 KAPPARIS: SUGGESTED Capparis spinosa. Confidence raised to 'certain' for C. spinosa L. in the broad (pre-segregate) sense; no source opened distinguishes C. spinosa s.str. from C. orientalis (Fraas' 'var. ovata' and 'C. rupestris' are not mapped to modern names here). (https://archive.org/details/BIUSante_dioscsprengelx02/page/n484/mode/1up ; https://archive.org/details/synopsisplantaru00fraa/page/n161/mode/1up)
notes: Greek capers are split into C. orientalis, C. sicula and C. zoharyi in the Greek checklist; GBIF keeps C. orientalis separate, so its records are pooled with C. spinosa s.l.
